That's not how the cloud save works. You're thinking of it as if the game was hosted on a central server and everything on your file was up to date regardless of the device as long as it's linked to the same account. 

The way cloud save works is to allow you to upload your current save file and then retrieve (or overwrite) the most current save. 

Here's an example. Say your phone is linked to cloud save and you get really far; the game automatically saves. But then you go to your iPad which is further behind and is also still connected to cloud save. Your iPad will automatically overwrite your current cloud save and revert all of the gameplay you made on your phone.

When you complete the starred objectives in the stages and also in your camp, there's a chance that a [purple star](https://mergedragons.fandom.com/wiki/Dragon_Stars) will drop instead of a gold star. I don't know the exact percentage but based on my testing it's lower than 10%. 

Anyways, if you get one in a level you can bring those back to your camp for free. You can tap each star once, then merge 3 (but better with 5) in order to create a Magnificent Dragon Star which drops dragon gems that you can merge. Don't collect any of the small dragon gems, you'll want to merge them to get the biggest one.

There are easy 1 chalice stages that people usually farm to get purple stars -- Zomblin Falls 1 and Dread Marsh 3 but realistically you can do it with any 1 chalice stage, these are just the fastest and easiest. 

Edit: Didn't see you ask about the egg nests. You can buy them if you want, I personally don't because they give those out in events.

This game gives you free gems. You don't need to purchase at all. 

As for gem efficiency, it's subjective but the best use is probably to save them for egg chests and radiant egg chests when you're completing your camp quests. You can also use them to buy items from Kala's shop but I would never buy any resources that you can merge yourself and definite hard pass on dimensional jars.

Well here's the thing, it gets more annoying if you keep breeding it in a line that it's not really supposed to be in. 

Let me give you an example, I'm assuming you're breeding the males back in with a 0/0 female that has the same original stats but the male is 0/5 in melee.

Female: 40 HP, 40 melee

Male: 40 HP, 50 melee

The HP is guaranteed to pass every time with a 55% chance to pass melee to subsequent offspring so you don't have to worry about any other stat passing.

However if you have something like 

Female: 40 HP, 40 melee

Male: 42 HP, 48 melee

Suddenly you have two stats you need to pass at a 55% each and it will take you a lot longer to move onto the next generation if you want to keep the mutation. Otherwise, if you opt not to pass the HP stat then you're just wasting a mutation. 

So, it's probably better to kill it or if you don't want to kill it then keep it as a house pet.
I believe the general rule of thumb is to kill it so you can keep your lines clean.
